title: Microsoft Teams: admin recommendations to enable agents for applications already in use
summary: The briefing's rollout, consent requirement and governance controls are supported. Licensing should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement, and two control paths should continue to the settings they describe.

claims.claim: Teams admin center recommends Teams apps and agents corresponding to applications already used in the organisation.
claims.quote: Admins can now use agent recommendations in the Teams admin center to identify Teams apps associated with applications your users already access with their work accounts.

claims.claim: ServiceNow, Workday and Jira are examples of the third-party applications covered by the notice.
claims.quote: Organizations often use third-party applications such as ServiceNow, Workday, Jira, and others, but the corresponding Microsoft Teams apps and agents may not be enabled for users.

claims.claim: Recommendations can be used to make an app available or deploy it to users who accessed the application with work accounts outside Teams.
claims.quote: From the recommendations, you can make an app available or deploy it to users in your organization who accessed or signed in to applications using their work accounts outside Teams.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Recommendations use sign-in activity data from Microsoft Purview Audit to identify applications accessed with work accounts.
claims.quote: To generate recommendations, the Teams admin center uses sign-in activity data from Microsoft Purview Audit to identify applications that users in your organization access with their work accounts.

claims.claim: Learn says the sign-in data is used only to recommend Teams agents.
claims.quote: The data is used only to recommend Teams agents associated with applications already used in your organization.

claims.claim: After opt-in, the list shows agents for applications users actively sign in to but do not yet have access to in Teams.
claims.quote: After you enable agent recommendations, the list shows Teams agents for applications that users in your organization actively sign in to but don't yet have access to in Teams.

claims.claim: The recommended list shows the number of users who sign in to each application but lack its agent in Teams.
claims.quote: User opportunity | The number of users who sign in to the application but don't have the agent available in Teams.

claims.claim: The list of users can be exported.
claims.quote: Select the download icon to export the list of users.

claims.claim: The recommended list shows whether each agent is unblocked or blocked in the organisation.
claims.quote: App status | Whether the agent is unblocked or blocked in your organization.

claims.claim: Recommended agents can be made available to everyone, specific users or groups, or users who recently accessed the application.
claims.quote: You can make a recommended agent available to everyone, specific users or groups, or users who recently accessed the related application.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].governs; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The workflow supports installing an agent for users or making it available for them to install themselves.
claims.quote: Select the users you want to: Install the agent for. Make the agent available to, so they can install it themselves.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Selecting users who access an application causes Teams admin center to create a security group for them.
claims.quote: When you select users who access an application in your organization, the Teams admin center creates a security group for those users.

claims.claim: The created group can be reviewed on the agent's Users and groups tab.
claims.quote: You can review the group on the Review and finish step and on the agent's Users and groups tab.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[2].note; Governance guidance; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Review and finish offers automatic addition of future users when they sign in to the application.
claims.quote: To automatically add future users to the group, select Add new users to this group when they sign in to the application on the Review and finish step for an app.

claims.claim: Automatic addition can be turned off to stop future application sign-ins adding users to the group.
claims.quote: Turn off automatic addition to prevent future users who sign in to the related application from being added automatically.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: At Permissions, a Teams Administrator must ask a Global Administrator to grant consent to the agent's permissions.
claims.quote: Review the required permissions and grant consent. If you're a Teams Administrator, ask a Global Administrator to grant consent.

claims.claim: Selections in the enablement workflow are applied when the administrator selects Apply.
claims.quote: Select Apply. Your selections are applied, and the agent is enabled for the specified users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Enablement workflow changes might take a few hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It might take a few hours for the changes to take effect.

claims.claim: Workflow selections are added to existing agent availability and installation settings.
claims.quote: These selections are added to the agent's existing availability and installation settings.

claims.claim: Existing assignments are not affected by the new workflow selections.
claims.quote: Existing assignments aren't affected.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Everyone availability includes all organisation users, new users and guests.
claims.quote: Everyone | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Specific users or groups availability excludes guests even if they are assigned.
claims.quote: Guests can't use the app if this option is selected and even if guests are assigned to the app.

claims.claim: Third-party agents have developer-provided service terms.
claims.quote: App developers provide customer support, publish updates and fixes, and share security, compliance, and service agreement details through the admin center app page.

claims.claim: Developers disclose agent data use and handling in terms of use and privacy policies.
claims.quote: In the terms of use and privacy policy of any agent or app, the app developer discloses what data their agent or app uses and how it handles the data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Developer terms and privacy-policy links are accessible on the app details page in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: This information is available on app developer's website and you can access the URLs in the app details page in Teams admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Developers can share paid-app pricing details through the app details experience.
claims.quote: Examples include compliance information, certifications, data handling practices, pricing details for paid apps, and setup instructions.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams Administrator is the documented role for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: All third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in Microsoft 365 Government GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: General app availability changes take up to 24 hours, and rarely up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect. In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.claim: Before unified app management migration, apps must be allowed in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps page.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow or block the agent or app in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: After unified app management migration, an app can be allowed in either admin centre.
claims.quote: If your organization is migrated to unified app management, allow or block the agent or app in Teams admin center or under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Scope
claims.claim: The notice addresses Teams administrators managing app and agent deployment and recommends communicating the change to those administrators.
claims.quote: Communicate the change to Teams administrators responsible for app governance and deployment.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Recommendations are opted out through Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Privacy and data usage.
claims.quote: To opt out of agent recommendations, go to Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Privacy and data usage. After you opt out, agent recommendations are no longer displayed.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Graph call for opting in or out of agent recommendations is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recommendations Privacy and data usage PowerShell Graph; MicrosoftTeams recommendations; Graph sign-in recommendations Teams consent. Read agents-existing-applications, Update-M365TeamsApp and beta teamsAppSettings; no recommendation-consent operation.

claims.claim: The recommended-agent workflow is reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > Filter by action > Agents from applications used in your org > Review > agent > Add users.
claims.quote: In the recommended agents list, select the agent, and then select Add users to proceed to the Users step.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Filter by action > Agents from applications used in your org > Review > agent > Add users > Users'. The Users step is where the cited page says to select users to install the agent for or make it available to.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets per-app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone

claims.claim: Automatic group addition is turned off on Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and Groups.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Manage apps > Select the app > Users and Groups tab. Turn off automatic addition to prevent future users who sign in to the related application from being added automatically.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the automatic-addition option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams automatic addition Graph; Teams automatic addition PowerShell; agent recommendations automatic. Read agents-existing-applications, Update-M365TeamsApp and beta teamsAppSettings; no parameter or property for this automatic-addition setting.

claims.claim: An app can be allowed or blocked through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes an app's tenant state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The bulk third-party-app availability control is under Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.
claims.fix: Complete controls[4].ui.path as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps > Let users install and use available apps by default'. The setting label is documented at the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the org-wide Third-party apps toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Third-party apps org-wide PowerShell settings. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp and beta teamsAppSettings. Custom-app and per-app operations do not document the org-wide third-party toggle.

claims.claim: Under app-centric management, the org-wide Third-party apps control does not override app-level configuration.
claims.quote: Post app centric management migration, these are unified into a single control that governs bulk availability for both new and existing third-party apps. This control doesn't override app-level configurations.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not apply to apps with individually saved availability settings.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you. All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually.

claims.claim: Org-wide app settings do not apply to blocked apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don't apply to: ... Any blocked apps.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no feature-specific licence is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace licensing.notes with 'Teams users need a Teams licence, except when joining meetings anonymously (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access). Microsoft has not published a licence or meter specific to agent recommendations as of November 2026.' Add that source and state the general Teams requirement in Cost and licensing while retaining the narrower feature-specific gap.

claims.claim: Administrators opt in on Teams apps > Manage apps using Agree and unlock insights on the Get relevant agent recommendations card.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps. On the Get relevant agent recommendations card, select Agree and unlock insights.
